units.function: Pure unit tests for classifying throttle-eligible Issue re-wakes and calculating a capped exponential cooldown from consecutive successful terminal Runs without Issue-visible progress.
units.dependencyDirection: Vitest -> pure issue-rewake-throttle policy; persistence, tenancy, queueing and clocks are supplied by callers.
units.keyDataModels: Wake reason, comment ID, requester actor type, explicit-resume/fresh-session flags; terminal Run ID/status/finishedAt; progress Run-ID set; new-input flag; throttle decision with streak/cooldown/nextAllowedAt.
units.lifecycle: Classify wake intent -> collect recent terminal Runs and progress/input facts -> reset on failure/progress/new input or increment no-progress streak -> block within capped cooldown -> allow retry after expiry.
units.testAssessment: All 14 pure tests passed in sandbox. Coverage is focused and deterministic across reason taxonomy, actor distinctions, explicit escalation, threshold/cap, expiry and reset conditions. It does not prove caller tenant isolation, ordering, clock behavior, durable decisions, concurrent queue idempotency, Connector delivery or safety-critical approval/emergency signal exemptions.
units.designRationale: Contain hot loops from Agents repeatedly waking on unchanged work without delaying genuine events, human input, explicit recovery or retry after actual failure.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs vendor-neutral backpressure for Agent loops and Connector retries while preserving immediate delivery of human decisions, approval deadlines, emergency stops and new evidence.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the pure policy, typed wake classes, capped exponential cooldown and progress/input/failure resets. Move reason strings to a versioned intent enum; bind evaluation to tenant/Work/Agent/Connector attempt; persist a throttle receipt and next-eligible time; enqueue atomically/idempotently; make HumanDecision, ApprovalGranted/Denied, EmergencyStop and permission-revocation non-throttleable invariants.
units.responsibilityConflict: The pure function cannot prove its supplied Runs/progress/input belong to the same Work or tenant, and Agent-authored explicit resume comments remain throttleable. A misclassified approval or recovery event could delay accountable-human control unless the surrounding contract defines safety-critical exemptions.
units.securityFindings: HIGH caller-boundary risk: no tenant/Work/Agent binding is expressible in the pure input. HIGH safety classification risk: correctness depends on an evolving string reason taxonomy. MEDIUM concurrency/durability gap: no persisted decision or enqueue idempotency evidence. MEDIUM clock/ordering gap: callers must provide correctly ordered Runs and trustworthy time. POSITIVE: human comments, explicit trusted resumes and event-shaped wakes bypass throttling; deterministic pure tests are strong.
